name: clmul
title: N-bit carry-less multiplier (product of polynomials over GF(2)): p = a (x) b on 2N-1 bits, without run-time + - *

banlist._comment: The task is to build a carry-less product from XOR/AND networks, so the arithmetic that would build the integer product (or the Kronecker trick: spread the bits, multiply as integers, read the parities) is banned at run time: * and the + - that Yosys merges into the same $macc/$alu cells. Run-time / % ** are banned in every task (since 2026-11-06, under the 2026-11-05 ruling that svGolf disallows a construct where Yosys departs from the standard): a zero divisor or a negative exponent makes an x from known operands, which ls-sv carries into decisions and Yosys builds as a defined value (score/banlist.py ALWAYS_BANNED). Constant arithmetic (parameter expressions, genvar indices) stays allowed.

references.note: the N x N array (AND partial products, XOR rows, no carries; mul_n's shape) proved with the sv_comb tactics (sv_structure with a lexicographic rank, sv_interface, sv_equations, sv_cover, sv_bridge) and the plain-Lean arithmetic in the file: the row invariant by induction and the collapse of the Spec's double sum; see PROVING.md, section 3.1

postsynth._comment: The fixed corners (130 vectors at N = 16), the harvested comparison constants and 500 seeded random vectors in FULL mode; the LIGHT mode runs light_vectors = 100 of them. ls-sv's run2 costs about 18 ms per vector (both schedules) on the array reference (330 vectors in 6.5 s of ls-sv time, 2026-11-01), so the budget is generous; the flat 32-bit baselines are 10 to 20 times slower per vector and are not checked at N = 32.
